## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vitakka Sutta* ("Thoughts", Iti 38; It 2.11, PTS It 31) is a discourse found in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. The text sets forth two distinct thoughts that habitually arise in the Buddha as he dwells delighting in non-ill will and seclusion.

  The sutta is additionally cited in exegetical canonical texts, including the *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), and *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 19).

No secondary literature in the reference dossier directly discusses Iti 38; matching search results under the title *Vitakka Sutta* discuss the *Dvedhāvitakka Sutta* (MN 19), while citations referencing "It. 38" cite page 38 of the Pali Text Society edition of the Itivuttaka (which contains Iti 44).
